title: AI & Machine Learning Privacy Security Checklist
metaDescription: Essential privacy checklist for AI tools like ChatGPT. Protect your data from machine learning surveillance and AI tracking with these steps.
intro: AI and machine learning tools collect vast amounts of personal data, often without clear disclosure. This checklist helps you protect your privacy when using AI services like ChatGPT, prevent unwanted data collection, and maintain control over your digital footprint.

items.task: Review and audit all AI service accounts
items.why: Many AI platforms collect chat history, preferences, and behavioral data that can reveal sensitive personal information.
items.howTo: Log into ChatGPT, Google AI, Microsoft Copilot, and other AI accounts. Review account settings, data collection policies, and delete unnecessary accounts you no longer use.

items.why: AI companies may store your conversations indefinitely unless you opt out or set deletion schedules.
items.howTo: In ChatGPT settings, turn off chat history. In Google AI products, visit myactivity.google.com to delete AI interactions and set auto-delete timers.

items.task: Opt out of AI model training
items.why: Your conversations may be used to train future AI models, potentially exposing your private information in AI responses to others.
items.howTo: In ChatGPT settings, disable 'Improve the model for everyone'. Check similar settings in other AI tools. Contact support if no clear opt-out exists.

items.task: Maximize privacy settings in AI tools
items.why: Default settings often prioritize data collection over privacy, sharing more information than necessary.
items.howTo: Enable privacy modes, disable data sharing, turn off personalization features, and restrict access to your other accounts when prompted by AI services.

items.task: Avoid sharing sensitive information with AI
items.why: Personal details, passwords, financial information, and private documents can be stored and potentially accessed by others.
items.howTo: Never input passwords, SSNs, financial details, or confidential work information. Use generic examples instead of real names, addresses, or personal situations.

items.task: Use Incognito Browser for AI interactions
items.why: Regular browsing leaves traces of your AI usage patterns and can link your AI activity to your other online behavior.
items.howTo: Open Incognito Browser before accessing AI tools. This prevents cookies and tracking scripts from building a profile of your AI usage across sessions.

items.why: Accumulated conversation history creates a detailed profile of your interests, problems, and thought patterns.
items.howTo: Monthly, delete chat histories in ChatGPT, Claude, Bard, and other AI tools. Use bulk delete options when available to clear all previous conversations.

items.task: Separate personal and work AI usage
items.why: Mixing contexts can lead to data leakage between personal and professional information, violating company policies or personal boundaries.
items.howTo: Use different accounts or browsers for work-related AI tasks. Consider using separate devices if your employer has strict AI usage policies.

items.why: Many websites now use AI-powered analytics and tracking that can identify you even in incognito mode through behavioral patterns.
items.howTo: Install uBlock Origin, Privacy Badger, or similar extensions. Enable strict tracking protection in your browser settings to block AI-powered fingerprinting attempts.

items.task: Secure voice assistants and smart devices
items.why: Alexa, Siri, and Google Assistant continuously collect audio data that feeds into AI systems and can be accessed by third parties.
items.howTo: Review voice recordings in device settings and delete them. Turn off always-listening features. Use push-to-talk mode instead of wake words when possible.

items.task: Opt out of facial recognition systems
items.why: AI-powered facial recognition is increasingly used by retailers, social media, and law enforcement to track your movements and behavior.
items.howTo: Contact major retailers to opt out of facial recognition. Adjust social media settings to prevent facial recognition tagging. Consider wearing masks in high-surveillance areas.

items.task: Remove your data from AI training datasets
items.why: Data brokers sell personal information to AI companies for model training, potentially including your photos, posts, and personal details.
items.howTo: Use services like DeleteMe or manually contact major data brokers. Send opt-out requests to companies like Clearview AI and PimEyes that specialize in facial recognition data.
